## Summary

**ADDIW** (Add Immediate Word extended to Long): Add data to destination.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `data + <ea> → <ea>` |
| Syntax | `ADDIW.L #<data>,<ea>` |
| Short | Add data to destination. |
| Description | Sign extend immediate word data to long and add to destination. Size is long. |
| Condition codes | see table |

### Condition codes

| X | N | Z | V | C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| * | * | * | * | * |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–6 | `0000011011` |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–0 | 16-bit word data |

### Example

```asm
    addiw.l    #$8001,d0
```

```text
ea d0: .. .. .. .. 00 12 34 56
Result:
ea d0: .. .. .. .. 00 11 B4 57
```

### Notes

- Replaces CALLM
- There is no subiw.l , just use a negative value with addiw.l

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no ADDIW. It is new on the 68080.
- ADDIW.L takes the place of the 68020 CALLM instruction (the original: "Replaces CALLM").

## Do / Don't

- DON'T look for SUBIW.L: it does not exist. Use ADDIW.L with a negative value.
